title: Blood Pressure Refill Check

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Hey, how can I help you today?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Oh, I'm just here to pick up my refill prescription. My name is Derek Jorgensen.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Oh, okay. Looks like I got it right here for you.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And that was the Ramipril, correct?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Ramipril, yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yeah, Ramipril. That's the 5 milligram strength.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Sounds right, yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Sounds right. Okay, so I got that one right here for you.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And since the last time you were in, have you had any problems with that medication?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No, it seems to be going great, yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay, for sure.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And have you had any changes in your prescription medication since the last time you came in?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I don't think so, no.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: We've taken this and two other things.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yeah, it looks like on file we have the atorvastatin and the hydrochlorothiazide. Is that correct?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yep, sounds right.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: That sounds right. The one, and what were you taking those two for?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I will have high blood pressure and high cholesterol, so yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay, and this one, was that also for the blood pressure?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: That was for the blood pressure as well.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay, so if you don't mind, we just take a few minutes here to make sure that's still working safely for you and still working for you. Does that sound good?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: That'd be great, yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay, for sure. So do you take your blood pressure at home at all?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yeah, I take it every morning. I get up and before I have my breakfast, I check it once.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Check it once? Okay, and can you explain the process of how you check it?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Oh, yeah, well, I think it was one of the pharmacists here told me to, they gave me a sheet on how to do it, so that's great.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: So I don't have any coffee or breakfast. I sit down and I make sure my feet are flat on the ground and I have been sitting, I sit there for a few minutes before I do it and I don't have my arm set up on a pillow and yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay, that's perfect. That sounds really great. And you mentioned you took it one time every morning?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Once a day, yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Once a day, okay. So just one recommendation I'd make to change. Everything you're doing sounds great, but I would recommend taking your blood pressure about three times rather than the one time, discarding that first value and just taking the average of the second two values.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And then that way it gives us a little bit more accurate reading of your blood pressure.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And what would you say your values normally are?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: You know, usually like 130 over 75 or 80, but yeah, it's been a little higher lately, maybe more like 140 is the higher number.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay. And sorry, I forgot to ask you earlier, do you take any over-the-counter medications that you can buy without a prescription?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Over-the-counter? Well, not usually, but lately I've been taking something for my knees, like some pain medication.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Oh, okay. And do you know what pain medication that was?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Ibuprofen.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Ibuprofen?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: 400 milligrams, yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay. And how often do you find you're taking that during the day?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Two or three times.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Two or three times? And that was for your knee pain?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And did you go to the doctor for that one?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And did the doctor suggest the ibuprofen?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Well, she just said go to the pharmacy and get something for your knees. She said I have arthritis, osteoarthritis.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: She took some x-rays and so she said, and so I just picked it myself to be honest, yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay. So you said your blood pressure has been a little bit higher lately. How long have you been taking that ibuprofen for?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: About a month maybe? Yeah. It's about a month ago the doctor said, yeah, you've got osteoarthritis.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay. So about a month. So yeah, the ibuprofen can interact a little bit with the Ramipril and it can lead to a bit of an increase in your blood pressure if you use it for a longer period of time.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Oh.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: So I recommend, have you ever tried Tylenol for your knee pain at all?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No, for sure. So we can take a look into getting you some Tylenol on your way out today.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Sure. So then, yeah, because you know, now that you mentioned it, I think my blood pressure has been a little bit higher in the last few weeks.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: That might be the cause of it. So we could look into that and keep maintaining your blood pressure because the values you told me, they sound great. They sound like they're in the right range.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: So it sounds like we want to keep it, keep things the way they are. So we could look into that after we're done here.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: That's great. Yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yeah. And do you take any herbal supplements or natural products?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Anything like that.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Any allergies to any medication?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And new medical conditions since last time you were in, other than the arthritis?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yeah, just that.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Just the arthritis?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Thank God, yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yeah. And do you have, do you find that you have any side effects that you attribute to the Ramipril at all?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I don't think so, no.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No. Any dizziness or lightheadedness at all?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No. Any lightheadedness from sitting to standing position?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No. Okay. I'm glad to hear that.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And how often would you wake up in the morning and realize you forgot to take your medication the day before?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Not very often. Like I'm pretty, pretty good. Yeah. Yeah. I think that almost never happens.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Never happens?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Pretty vigilant, yeah.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay. That's great. I'm glad to hear that.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And do you have any questions for me today about the Ramipril or any of the other medications?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yeah. You know, the only thing when you said take my blood pressure three times. So should I take it like breakfast, lunch, supper or?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Oh, sorry. Yeah. So yeah, I would recommend taking it three times in a row. I know it might hurt your arm or...

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Oh, like back to back.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Back to back is what we, the best way to do it.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: And then ignore the first one.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Right. Ignore the first one. Take the average of the second two.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I'll do the second two. Okay. I can do that.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yeah, for sure. Any other questions for me today?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: That's it. No, thank you.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Well, if you think of anything, give us a call. We're always here.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay. I'll go grab some Tylenol.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Great. Sounds good.
